source: RedAmon Bug Bounty Coverage 7.5.0 taxonomy (2026-10-30), adapted as the CyberBox methodology spine

payout_scale.note: payout_rank 1..5 maps $..$$$$$ — what the class actually pays once dupe saturation and triage drift are priced in. Runs OPPOSITE to priority: a P5 primitive can be $$$$$ inside a chain.

families.name: Information Disclosure and Secrets
families.note: The finding is the credential, not the disclosure.

families.name: HTTP Desync, Caching and Proxy
families.note: Front-end/back-end parsing disagreement; cache keyed wrong.

families.name: API and GraphQL Specific
families.note: Object- and function-level authz on machine surface.

families.name: Infrastructure, DNS and Cloud
families.note: Dangling records, metadata, misconfigured buckets.

families.name: OAuth, SSO and Federation
families.note: redirect_uri, state, token confusion — account takeover surface.

families.name: AI and LLM Attack Surface
families.note: Indirect prompt injection into tool-calling agents (CWE-1427) fastest-growing scoped surface.

families.name: Supply Chain and CI/CD
families.note: Dependency confusion, runner poisoning, build-system compromise.

families.name: Cryptography and Token Handling
families.note: JWT confusion, weak secrets, predictable tokens.

families.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
families.note: Value is reaching cloud metadata / internal services, not the DNS ping.

families.name: Server-Side Injection
families.note: SQLi / RCE / SSTI at the top.

families.name: XML, Deserialization and Parser Attacks
families.note: XXE, insecure deserialization, parser differentials.

families.name: Business Logic, Race Conditions and Workflow
families.note: State machines, TOCTOU, idempotency, value extraction.

families.name: Authentication and Session Management
families.note: Password reset, session fixation, 2FA bypass.

families.name: Broken Access Control and Authorization
families.note: IDOR / BOLA / BFLA — highest paid family by concentration.

families.name: File Upload and Path Handling
families.note: Unrestricted upload, path traversal, LFI.

families.name: Cross-Site Scripting and Client-Side Injection
families.note: Highest report VOLUME, not highest payout; dupe-heavy standalone.

families.name: Cross-Origin and Browser Trust
families.note: CORS, postMessage, cookie scope, CSP bypass.

families.name: Client-Side Request and Path Manipulation
families.note: CSPT, client-side path traversal into trusted fetches.

families.name: Content Spoofing, Redirects and Impersonation
families.note: Open redirect, dangling markup — chain fuel, weak alone.

families.name: Denial of Service and Resource Abuse
families.note: Mostly out of scope; narrow exceptions, isolated instances only.

families.name: Adjacent scope worth knowing
families.note: Mobile, thick-client, binary surface bordering web scope.

families.name: Frontier classes, 2025 to 2026
families.note: Newest techniques: agentic AI, HTTP/1.1 desync endgame, CSPT2CSRF.

families.name: Chains that turn a medium into a critical
families.note: The escalation catalog. Most large payouts are 2-3 ordinary findings stacked.

families.name: Commonly closed as informational
families.note: Never report standalone — only inside a chain or when the program explicitly asks.

families.name: Reporting checklist
families.note: What moves a finding to the top of the triage queue.

classes.name: Disclosure of secrets for a publicly accessible asset
classes.signal: Live provider key / token reachable without auth.

classes.name: Disclosure of secrets for an internal asset
classes.signal: Credential for an internal-only system.

classes.name: Secrets in JavaScript bundles
classes.signal: Keys inlined at build time; grep provider formats and identifiers containing secret/token/key/password/apiKey.

classes.name: Disclosure of known public information / intentionally public samples
classes.signal: Sample/demo data; usually informational.

classes.name: IDOR reading another user's object (BOLA)
classes.signal: Object id in path/body swaps to another tenant's record; read one record, not the table.

classes.name: IDOR writing/modifying another user's object
classes.signal: Mutation accepts a foreign object id and persists.

classes.name: Broken function-level authorization (BFLA)
classes.signal: Admin/privileged action reachable by a lower role; test the same action across roles.

classes.name: Horizontal/vertical privilege escalation via mass assignment
classes.signal: Role/owner field accepted on an update it shouldn't be.

classes.name: Account takeover via password reset flaw
classes.signal: Reset token predictable, host-header-poisoned, or trusts an attacker-controlled email.

classes.name: 2FA/OTP bypass
classes.signal: OTP brute inside rate limit, response differential, or step skippable.

classes.name: Session fixation / not invalidated on credential change
classes.signal: Old session still valid after password/2FA/email change.

classes.name: OAuth redirect_uri accepts attacker value
classes.signal: redirect_uri validation loose; code/token leaks to attacker origin.

classes.name: Missing/weak state parameter (OAuth CSRF)
classes.signal: No per-request state; attacker binds their account.

classes.name: SQL injection
classes.signal: Error/boolean/time differential on a param reaching a query without prepare.

classes.name: Server-side template injection (SSTI)
classes.signal: Template expression evaluates in a response field (e.g. {{7*7}} -> 49).

classes.name: OS command injection / RCE
classes.signal: Shell metacharacters reach a command; OOB confirms blind.

classes.name: SSRF reaching cloud metadata (IMDS)
classes.signal: Request reaches 169.254.169.254 and returns role credentials.

classes.name: Blind SSRF (OOB only)
classes.signal: OOB DNS/HTTP callback, no internal reach yet — chain fuel.

classes.name: Race condition on a limit (coupon/withdrawal/balance)
classes.signal: Parallel requests exceed a server-enforced limit; measure state, not just status.

classes.name: Business-logic workflow bypass
classes.signal: Step skippable, price/quantity tamperable, state transition out of order.

classes.name: Stored XSS (authenticated context)
classes.signal: Payload persists and executes in another user's session.

classes.name: Reflected XSS
classes.signal: Param reflected into HTML/JS sink without encoding; dupe-heavy alone.

classes.name: Self-XSS
classes.signal: Only fires in attacker's own session — report only in a chain.

classes.name: Subdomain takeover
classes.signal: Dangling CNAME to an unclaimed service.

classes.name: Unrestricted file upload to web-exec path
classes.signal: Upload reaches a path the server executes.

classes.name: Path traversal / LFI
classes.signal: ../ reaches files outside the intended root.

classes.name: Indirect prompt injection into a tool-calling agent
classes.signal: Untrusted content steers an agent's tool calls (fetch/exec).

classes.name: HTTP request smuggling / desync
classes.signal: Front-end/back-end disagree on request boundaries.

classes.name: Web cache deception
classes.signal: Authenticated page cached under a static-looking path.

classes.name: Client-side path traversal (CSPT)
classes.signal: Client builds a fetch path from user input into a trusted API call.

classes.name: Open redirect
classes.signal: redirect/next param sends user off-origin; chain fuel, weak alone.

classes.name: Dependency confusion (internal package name)
classes.signal: Internal package name resolvable from a public registry.

informational_standalone: Missing security headers alone (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options)
Self-XSS with no delivery mechanism
Clickjacking on a page with no state-changing action
CSRF on logout, language switch, or a trivial preference
CSRF token not unique per request
Missing SPF or DMARC on a non-sending domain; spoofing that only reaches spam
Absence of rate limiting with no cost, lockout or data reached
Version and banner disclosure, software versions in response headers
Weak TLS configuration, certificate errors, no forward secrecy, mixed content
Open redirect on its own (out of scope on many programs)
User enumeration on its own (closed on most consumer platforms)
Autocomplete enabled, save-password allowed, plaintext password field, autocorrect enabled
No password policy, weak password policy, long session timeout, concurrent logins
Session not invalidated server-side only on logout; not invalidated on email or 2FA change
Reset token with a long expiry, or not invalidated after login or after a new request
OPTIONS or TRACE enabled
Internal IP disclosure, full path disclosure, descriptive stack trace
Publicly accessible robots.txt, GraphQL introspection enabled, missing SRI
Cookie scoped to the parent domain, missing HttpOnly on a non-session cookie
Missing CAA, missing DNSSEC, bitsquatting
A public CVE matched by version number only, with no verification on the target
Unpatched JavaScript libraries with no reachable sink
Raw, unvalidated scanner output (the single most common reason a report is closed)
Best-practice recommendations with no attack narrative
reporting_checklist: One finding per report, with the class named the way the program's taxonomy names it
Impact stated first, in the terms the business cares about: whose data, how many, what action, reversible or not
Reproduction that works from a clean session, with two accounts where the bug needs two
Minimal proof, not maximal exploitation. Read one record, not the table. Enumerate permissions read-only, never escalate further than needed to prove the class
The chain written out when it is a chain, with each link's own severity noted
No third-party or out-of-scope collateral, no DoS unless explicitly permitted, no data exfiltration beyond proof, nothing published
A concrete fix suggestion. It shortens triage and it is what separates a researcher from a scanner
